readings.title: A Plea Denied
readings.subtitle: Moses’ Final Appeal to Enter the Land
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 3:21] And I commanded Yehoshua at that time, saying, ‘Your eyes have seen all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> has done to these two kings. <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does the same to all the reigns which you are passing over. [22] Do not fear them, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> <dn>He</dn> is <dn>the One</dn> fighting for you.’ [23] And I pleaded with <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> at that time, saying, [24] ‘O <dn>Master YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>You</dn> have begun to show <dn>Your</dn> servant <dn>Your</dn> greatness and <dn>Your</dn> strong hand, for who is a mighty one in the heavens or on earth who does according to <dn>Your</dn> works and according to <dn>Your</dn> might? [25] I pray, let me pass over and see the good land beyond the Yarden, this good hill country, and Lebanon.’ [26] But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was enraged with me because of you, and would not listen to me. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>‘Enough of that! Speak no more to <dn>Me</dn> about this matter.</dq> [27] <dq>Go up to the top of Pisgah, and lift up your eyes westward, and northward, and southward, and eastward, and look with your eyes, for you do not pass over this Yarden.</dq> [28] <dq>But command Yehoshua, and strengthen him and encourage him, for he shall pass over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit the land which you see.’</dq> [29] So we dwelt in the valley opposite Bĕyth Pe’or.

readings.title: The Path of Life
readings.subtitle: Obedience to the Laws and Right-Rulings
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 4:1] And now, O Yisra’ĕl, listen to the laws and the right-rulings which I am teaching you to do, so that you live, and shall go in and possess the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of your fathers is giving you. [2] Do not add to the Word which I command you, and do not take away from it, so as to guard the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> which I am commanding you. [3] Your eyes have seen what <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> did at Ba’al Pe’or, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> has destroyed from your midst all the men who followed Ba’al Pe’or. [4] But you who are clinging to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> are all alive today. [5] See, I have taught you laws and right-rulings, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>my Elohim</dn> commanded me, to do thus in the land which you are going to possess. [6] And you shall guard and do them, for this is your wisdom and your understanding before the eyes of the peoples who hear all these laws, and they shall say, ‘Only a wise and understanding people is this great nation!’ [7] For what great nation is there which has <dn>Elohim</dn> so near to it, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>our Elohim</dn> is to us, whenever we call on <dn>Him</dn>? [8] And what great nation is there that has such righteous laws and right-rulings as all this Torah which I set before you today? [9] Only, guard yourself, and guard your life diligently, lest you forget the words your eyes have seen, and lest they leave your heart all the days of your life. And you shall make them known to your children and your grandchildren. [10] The day you stood before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> in Ḥorĕḇ, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>‘Assemble the people to <dn>Me</dn>, and <dn>I</dn> make them hear <dn>My</dn> words, so that they learn to fear <dn>Me</dn> all the days they live on the earth, and teach them to their children.’</dq> [11] And you came near and stood at the foot of the mountain, and the mountain burned with fire to the midst of the heavens – darkness, cloud, and thick darkness. [12] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to you out of the midst of the fire. You heard a voice of words, but saw no form, only a voice. [13] And <dn>He</dn> made known to you <dn>His</dn> covenant which <dn>He</dn> commanded you to do, the Ten Words, and <dn>He</dn> wrote them on two tablets of stone. [14] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded me at that time to teach you laws and right-rulings, for you to do them in the land which you pass over to possess.

readings.title: The Formless Voice
readings.subtitle: Warning Against the Corruption of Idolatry
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 4:15] Therefore, guard your lives diligently, for you saw no form when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to you at Ḥorĕḇ out of the midst of the fire, [16] lest you should corrupt yourselves and shall make for yourselves a carved image in the form of any figure – the likeness of male or female, [17] the likeness of any beast that is on the earth or the likeness of any winged bird that flies in the heavens, [18] the likeness of any creature that creeps on the ground or the likeness of any fish that is in the waters under the earth, [19] and lest you lift up your eyes to the heavens, and shall see the sun, and the moon, and the stars – all the host of the heavens – and you be drawn away and shall bow down to them and serve them, which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> has allotted to all the peoples under all the heavens. [20] But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has taken you and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Mitsrayim, to be <dn>His</dn> people, an inheritance, as it is today. [21] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was enraged with me because of your words, and swore that I should not pass over the Yarden, and that I should not enter the good land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> is giving you as an inheritance. [22] For I am to die in this land, I am not passing over the Yarden, but you are passing over, and shall possess that good land. [23] Guard yourselves, lest you forget the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> which <dn>He</dn> made with you, and shall make for yourselves a carved image in the form of anything which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> has forbidden you. [24] For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> is a consuming fire, a jealous <dn>Ěl</dn>. [25] When you bring forth children and grandchildren and have grown old in the land, and shall corrupt yourselves and make a carved image in the form of anything, and shall do what is evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> to provoke <dn>Him</dn> to humble you, [26] I call the heavens and the earth to witness against you today, that you shall soon utterly perish from the land which you pass over the Yarden to possess. You shall not prolong your days in it, but shall be utterly destroyed. [27] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall scatter you among the peoples, and you shall be left few in number among the gentiles where <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> drives you. [28] And there you shall serve mighty ones, the work of men’s hands, wood and stone, which neither see nor hear nor eat nor smell. [29] But from there you shall seek <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn>, and shall find <dn>Him</dn> if you seek <dn>Him</dn> with all your heart and with all your life. [30] In your distress, when all these words shall come upon you in the latter days, then you shall return to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> and shall obey <dn>His</dn> voice. [31] For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> is a compassionate <dn>Ěl</dn>, <dn>He</dn> does not forsake you nor destroy you, nor forget the covenant of your fathers which <dn>He</dn> swore to them.

readings.title: A Nation Set Apart
readings.subtitle: The Unique Greatness of YeHoVaH
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 4:32] For ask now of the days that are past, which were before you, since the day that <dn>Elohim</dn> created man on the earth, and ask from one end of the heavens to the other, whether there has been a thing as great as this, or has been heard like it? [33] Has a people heard the voice of <dn>Elohim</dn> speaking out of the midst of the fire, as you have heard, and lived? [34] Or has an <dn>Elohim</dn> tried to go and take for <dn>Himself</dn> a nation from the midst of another nation, by trials, and by signs, and by wonders, and by battle, and by a strong hand, and by an outstretched arm, and by great fears, according to all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> did for you in Mitsrayim before your eyes? [35] You have been shown it, to know that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Himself</dn> is <dn>Elohim</

showed you <dn>His</dn> great fire, and you heard <dn>His</dn> words out of the midst of the fire. [37] And because <dn>He</dn> loved your fathers, therefore <dn>He</dn> chose their seed after them, and brought you out of Mitsrayim with <dn>His</dn> Presence, with <dn>His</dn> great power, [38] to drive out from before you nations greater and stronger than you, to bring you in, to give you their land as an inheritance, as it is today. [39] And you shall know today, and shall take it to your heart that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Himself</dn> is <dn>Elohim</dn> in the heavens above and on the earth beneath; there is no one else. [40] And you shall guard <dn>His</dn> laws and <dn>His</dn> commands which I command you today, so that it is well with you and with your children after you, and so that you prolong your days on the soil which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> is giving you for all time.

readings.title: East of the Yarden
readings.subtitle: Cities of Refuge and the Border of the Torah
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 4:41] Then Mosheh separated three cities on this side of the Yarden, toward the rising of the sun, [42] for the manslayer to flee there, who killed his neighbour unintentionally, not having hated him in time past, and that by fleeing to one of these cities he might live: [43] Betser in the wilderness on the plateau for the Re’uḇĕnites, and Ramoth in Gil’aḏ for the Gaḏites, and Golan in Bashan for the Menashshites. [44] And this is the Torah which Mosheh set before the children of Yisra’ĕl. [45] These are the witnesses, and the laws, and the right-rulings which Mosheh spoke to the children of Yisra’ĕl after they came out of Mitsrayim, [46] on this side of the Yarden, in the valley opposite Bĕyth Pe’or, in the land of Siḥon king of the Amorites, who dwelt at Ḥeshbon, whom Mosheh and the children of Yisra’ĕl smote after they came out of Mitsrayim. [47] And they took possession of his land and the land of Og̱ king of Bashan, two kings of the Amorites, who were on this side of the Yarden, toward the rising of the sun, [48] from Ar’o’ĕr, which is on the edge of the wadi Arnon, even to Mount Siyon, that is Ḥermon, [49] and all the Araḇah on this side of the Yarden eastward, as far as the Sea of the Araḇah, below the slopes of Pisgah.

readings.title: The Covenant at Ḥorĕḇ
readings.subtitle: The Ten Words Repeated
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 5:1] And Mosheh called all Yisra’ĕl, and said to them, “Hear, O Yisra’ĕl, the laws and right-rulings which I speak in your hearing today, and you shall learn them and guard to do them. [2] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>our Elohim</dn> made a covenant with us in Ḥorĕḇ. [3] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> did not make this covenant with our fathers, but with us, those who are here today, all of us alive. [4] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke with you face to face on the mountain from the midst of the fire. [5] I stood between <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and you at that time, to declare to you the Word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for you were afraid because of the fire, and you did not go up the mountain, saying: [6] <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> who brought you out of the land of Mitsrayim, out of the house of bondage.</dq> [7] <dq>You have no other mighty ones against <dn>My</dn> face.</dq> [8] <dq>You do not make for yourself a carved image, any likeness of which is in the heavens above, or which is in the earth beneath, or which is in the waters under the earth,</dq> [9] <dq>you do not bow down to them nor serve them. For <dn>I</dn>, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn>, am a jealous <dn>Ěl</dn>, visiting the crookedness of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate <dn>Me</dn>,</dq> [10] <dq>but showing kindness to thousands, to those who love <dn>Me</dn> and guard <dn>My</dn> commands.</dq> [11] <dq>You do not bring the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> to naught, for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does not leave him unpunished who brings <dn>His</dn> Name to naught.</dq> [12] <dq>Guard the Sabbath day, to set it apart, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> commanded you.</dq> [13] <dq>Six days you labour, and shall do all your work,</dq> [14] <dq>but the seventh day is a Sabbath to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn>. You do not do any work – you, nor your son, nor your daughter, nor your male servant, nor your female servant, nor your ox, nor your donkey, nor any of your cattle, nor your stranger who is within your gates, so that your male servant and your female servant rest as you do.</dq> [15] <dq>And you shall remember that you were a servant in the land of Mitsrayim, and that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> brought you out from there by a strong hand and by an outstretched arm. Therefore <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> commanded you to observe the Sabbath day.</dq> [16] <dq>Respect your father and your mother, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> has commanded you, so that your days are prolonged, and so that it is well with you on the soil which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</dn> is giving you.</dq> [17] <dq>You do not murder.</dq> [18] <dq>You do not commit adultery.</dq> [19] <dq>You do not steal.</dq> [20] <dq>You do not bear false witness against your neighbour.</dq> [21] <dq>You do not covet your neighbour’s wife, nor do you desire your neighbour’s house, his field, nor his male servant, nor his female servant, his ox, nor his donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbour.’</dq>

readings.title: The Fear of the People
readings.subtitle: The Request for a Mediator
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 5:22] These Words <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to all your assembly, in the mountain from the midst of the fire, of the cloud, and of the thick darkness, with a loud voice, and <dn>He</dn> added no more. And <dn>He</dn> wrote them on two tablets of stone and gave them to me. [23] And it came to be, when you heard the voice from the midst of the darkness, while the mountain was burning with fire, that you came near to me, all the heads of your tribes and your elders. [24] And you said, ‘See, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>our Elohim</dn> has shown us <dn>His</dn> esteem and <dn>His</dn> greatness, and we have heard <dn>His</dn> voice from the midst of the fire. Today we have seen that <dn>Elohim</
speaking from the midst of the fire, as we have, and lived? [27] You go near and hear all that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>our Elohim</

says to you, and we shall listen and do it.’ [28] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> heard the voice of your words when you spoke to me, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to me, <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> have heard the voice of the words of this people which they have spoken to you. They have done well in all that they have spoken.</dq> [29] <dq>Oh, that they had such a heart in them, to fear <dn>Me</dn> and to guard all <dn>My</dn> commands always, so that it might be well with them and with their children forever!</dq> [30] <dq>Go, say to them, “Return to your tents.”</dq> [31] <dq>But you, stand here by <dn>Me</dn>, and let <dn>Me</dn> speak to you all the commands, and the laws, and the right-rulings which you are to teach them, and they shall do them in the land which <dn>I</dn> am giving them to possess.’</dq> [32] So you shall guard to do as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>your Elohim</
has commanded you, so that you live and it be well with you, and you prolong your days in the land which you possess.
